description: Team Riley default for Astro sites deployed on Netlify. Patch and minor updates auto-merge once the Netlify deploy preview is green; majors and the shared Shopify engine wait for a human.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly lockfile refresh: re-resolves every transitive dependency to the newest version its range allows, which is what `npm audit fix` does by hand. Renovate does not otherwise touch transitive deps, so this is the sweep that clears Dependabot alerts. Auto-merges on a green Netlify preview.

packageRules.description: Patch and minor updates auto-merge, but only after every status check (the Netlify deploy preview) passes. A repo with no checks keeps the PR open for a human.
Astro and its integrations move together.
Tailwind and its plugins move together.
Alpine and its plugins move together.
Test tooling moves together and is safe to auto-merge on green.

Major versions change config (Tailwind 3 to 4, Astro majors) and usually cannot build without a hand migration. They are listed on the Dependency Dashboard and only become a PR (and a Netlify preview build) when a person ticks the box. Security fixes that need a major still open on their own.
GitHub Actions updates, majors included, are routine: no dashboard approval, auto-merge once the repo's checks pass. A repo with no checks keeps the PR open.

The shared Shopify engine is pinned to a git tag on purpose. A new tag is listed on the Dependency Dashboard and becomes a PR only when ticked (Mend's runner cannot fetch git dependencies, so the PR needs its lockfile updated by hand anyway). Never auto-merged.

Sites still on @lucide/astro 0.x stay below 1.0: 1.x removed the brand icons (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube) their footers use. Sites already on 1.x update normally, which they need because only newer 1.x releases accept Astro 7.
No PRs for the package.json engines field. Netlify takes its Node version from netlify.toml / .nvmrc, so raising the engines floor changes nothing and only adds PRs.
